text:
incident-bot: ALERT: Service routing health-check flap detected between regions (us-east <-> us-west <-> eu). spike in 502s and probe failures. auto-escalation to on-call. metric: health_fail_rate > 8% over 3m for routing-policy=smart-fallback. See https://monitoring.redwood/graphs/abc123 :rotating_light:

emma: Paging SRE oncall @raj — I'm getting the automated page. Observed customer errors increasing since 17:02 UTC. Root looks like probes toggling healthy/unhealthy between us-east/us-west/eu and triggering cross-region fallback churn.

raj: On it. I saw the same in infra dashboard. Starting live triage. Can someone call out if there's an active rollout of routing policy? @lena?

lena: Not from runtime team. We last touched smart-fallback rules yesterday (small tweak to prefer local) but no deploys in last 12h. I'll pull routing policy git history.

carl: Support flagged a major customer (Neptune Inc) seeing 5xxs on inference calls. Support ticket #SUP-1982. They reported multiple retries and higher latency.

mike-ops: Adding preliminary impact: ~3.4k requests/min, error spike to 6% 5xx, customer-facing errors concentrated on embeddings route and chat. Could be wrong model variant landing in fallback region.

emma: OK mitigation plan — 1) pause cross-region fallback for smart-fallback policy (temporary) 2) increase health-check debounce from 30s -> 90s 3) notify customers. Who can flip policy? @raj or infra runbook?

raj: I can flip. Taking lead. Executing temporary policy change to stop cross-region failover while we stabilize. Running: 
```bash
# temporarily disable cross-region fallback for smart-fallback
redwoodctl routing update-policy --name smart-fallback --allow-cross-region false --reason "mitigate flap 1719987654"
```

incident-bot: ACTION LOGGED: redwoodctl routing update-policy --name smart-fallback --allow-cross-region false --by raj --at 17:08:42 UTC -- change_id ch_9f3a

lena: While that's running I'll increase health debounce on the probe manager: 
```yaml
probe_manager:
  check_interval: 10s
  failure_threshold: 9   # was 3
  success_threshold: 3
  debounce_window: 90s   # was 30s
```
Applying to probe-manager in eu/us-west/us-east via canary first.

mike-ops: Rolling config to probe-manager canary in us-west (one pod) now. Command: `kubectl -n infra rollout restart deploy/probe-manager --selector=canary=true`

emma: Support, please send an advisory to Neptune: short note that we're mitigating routing health-check churn and temporarily preventing cross-region failover to reduce customer errors. Provide ETA ~30-45m.

support-bot: Message queued to customer Neptune Inc: "We're currently mitigating transient routing issues that may affect request reliability. We're applying temporary controls and will update within 45 minutes." (ticket SUP-1982)

raj: Observability update: after disable, cross-region handoffs dropped 94% in the last 2m. Error rate trending down from 6% -> 1.9%. Still seeing some residual 502s tied to stuck KV cache entries on runtime nodes that had rapid probe toggles.

lena: Confirming – a few runtimes ended up with stale prefix caches when they got quickly demoted/promoted. Working on a selective KV cache invalidate for nodes that flapped. Plan: run targeted cache clear for nodes with last_probe_change < 6m and health=false.

raj: Command to identify flapped nodes: 
```bash
redwoodctl nodes list --filter "probe_change_minutes>1 AND probe_change_minutes<10" --fields id,region,last_probe_state
```
Then clear caches: 
```bash
for id in $(...); do redwoodctl runtime exec --node $id --cmd "runtime-cli cache clear --prefix=kv"; done
```

incident-bot: Runbook step executed by raj: targeted cache clears started 17:15:03 UTC.

mike-ops: After cache clears and debounce increase, 5xx rate back to baseline ~0.4%. Latency normalized for most customers. Neptune support reports a few successful retries, will monitor.

carl: Any sign of a config bug that could cause probes to flip-loop across regions? Need to check probe TTLs and regional health scoring. Also check model-variant mapping — some requests may have been routed to a variant not available in fallback region and returned 5xx.

lena: Quick check: model catalog mappings show correct variant availability. I see a minor mismatch in the fallback policy rule for embeddings: fallback_order included eu before us-west in an older rule unintentionally. That could cause a hop between eu and us-west when us-east toggles. Searching git history now.

raj: Good catch. If there's a stale rule, we should make that explicit in the postmortem. For now we've disabled cross-region fallback globally for smart-fallback; we'll re-enable only after audit and a safe rollout.

emma: Handing pager to @raj for incident lead. I'm going offline to coordinate customer comms and SOC updates. Raj, you're primary; Lena, continue with runtime analysis. Mike, watch infra rollout. Carl, coordinate post-incident comm.

raj: Taking lead. Will keep updates in thread. Next steps: 1) finish probe debounce rollout to all regions (target 17:30) 2) finish KV cache clears (in progress) 3) audit routing rules for unintended fallback_order entries 4) prepare canary to re-enable cross-region fallback with strict fallback_order and rate limits.

incident-bot: METRICS: at 17:22 UTC error_rate 5xx=0.9% (down from 6%), fallback_count down 96%.

lena: Found the bad rule — created 2025-08-11 in repo routing/policies.yaml, entry id rpl_44c had eu listed ahead of us-west for embeddings if local missing. I raised PR to correct order and added explicit comment: "prefer nearest regional fallback unless model limited". PR: https://git.internal/routing/pulls/4728

mike-ops: Probe debounce rollout completed to all regions at 17:29 UTC. KV cache clears finished at 17:31 UTC. Systems stable in last 6m.

carl: Customer impact summary for initial incident window (17:02–17:28 UTC): approx 3,200 requests/min, aggregated ~2.8k failed requests total across affected customers, peak error rate 6%. Major customer Neptune saw ~0.8% of their requests fail. We're offering credit; support is following up.

emma: Good. Raj, are you comfortable we can re-enable cross-region fallback with the corrected policy and slower debounce? Suggest canary re-enable to us-east only first with rate cap.

raj: Yes. Plan: re-enable cross-region fallback for us-east only with rate cap 0.5% and strict fallback_order. Command: 
```bash
redwoodctl routing update-policy --name smart-fallback --allow-cross-region true --regions us-east --rate-cap 0.005 --fallback-order us-west,eu --reason "canary re-enable post-mitigation 1719987654"
```
We'll monitor for 10m.

incident-bot: ACTION LOGGED: policy re-enable canary started by raj at 17:36:11 UTC (ch_9f3b). Rollout to us-east canary nodes.

mike-ops: Can confirm canary re-enable looks clean. No spike in fallthroughs. Error rate steady at 0.3%.

support-bot: Neptune updated: "Issue mitigated; we will follow up if you see anything else. Thank you for the quick response." (SUP-1982)

raj: After 12m of stable canary I will gradually roll the corrected policy to other regions. If anything reoccurs we'll immediately flip allow-cross-region false.

emma: OK handing back to runbook owner for postmortem. Please capture timeline, root cause (stale fallback_order + aggressive health debounce + probe sensitivity), corrective actions (policy fix PR, probe debounce default increase, safer rollout checklist). Assigning follow-ups: Routing policy test coverage (lena), probe-manager default debounce change (mike-ops), customer comm writeup (carl).

lena: Will open a postmortem doc and link PRs. Drafting now.

incident-bot: INCIDENT RESOLVED: auto-close scheduled after 24h if no regressions. summary_id: inc_20260315_1719987654

raj: Final note — learned that small policy mismatches + low debounce can create oscillations that cascade across regions. Recommend adding synthetic chaos tests for fallback churn and a pre-deploy safety check that rejects fallback_order changes without explicit sign-off.

emma: Agreed. Thanks team. Closing on-call. :white_check_mark:
